_comment: Curated mappings from a Helix career to a National Careers Service job
profile, for cases the title matcher cannot decide on its own.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The matcher accepts only an exact normalised title
match. 737 public NCS profiles exist and only 54 matched that way, so most
careers fall back to a derived estimate. Every entry added here promotes one
career from a derived estimate to career-specific evidence on the next run.
It is the single highest-value piece of data work available in this project.
HOW TO ADD ONE. Open docs/MARKET-DATA-AUDIT.md and find the section
'Alias candidates for human review'. Each row gives a Helix career, the
external profile it nearly matched, and the score. If the two really are the
same job, add an entry below:
"<normalised helix title>": "<ncs profile slug>"
The key must be the title as title_matcher.normalise() produces it:
lowercased, punctuation stripped, curated abbreviations expanded. Check it
with:
python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools'); \
from market_data.title_matcher import normalise; \
print(normalise('Andrology Scientist'))"
The value is the slug from the profile URL:
https://nationalcareers.service.gov.uk/job-profiles/<slug>
WHAT NOT TO ADD. Never alias a seniority variant to its base profile.
'Senior Biomedical Scientist' is not the same job as 'Biomedical scientist',
and mapping it would publish an entry-grade salary range as a career-specific
fact about a senior post. The matcher rejects these deliberately and the
audit does not list them as candidates. Adding one by hand defeats the check.
Never add an alias to make coverage look better. A transparent derived
estimate is better than a confident wrong one, and doing nothing here is
always a safe choice.
AFTER EDITING. Re-run the pipeline and check what changed:
python tools/market_data/enrich.py --all --offline --dry-run
python tools/market_data/validate.py
The offline dry run costs no API quota. Removing an alias is equally safe:
the career simply returns to a derived estimate.
